exact_statement: Determine whether there is an absolute constant C such that, for every integer n>=1, sum over primes p<=n with p not dividing binomial(2n,n) of 1/p is at most C.
scope_notes: The target is a single absolute constant uniform in every integer n; density-one, average, or C log log n estimates do not close it.
Kummer/Legendre equivalences may be used, but every endpoint convention for p=2 and p^j>2n must be replayed exactly.
Finite maxima and CRT searches are falsifiers only; they cannot establish boundedness without an all-n scale argument.
All expensive enumeration and proof-search processes must run through /home/biostar/work/projects/openmath/bin/openmath-memory-guard.
